Hi Guneet / procurement team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — great alignment on the POC scope. Attached is the latest SOW (EdgeCloud_SOW_v3.pdf) and a simple pricing sheet. To help them get through procurement quickly, I built in a channel concession that brings the first-year TCV down by 40% off list on the initial POC order.

Quick asks:
- Guneet: can you confirm procurement timeline (PO or signature target date)?
- Internal: Marissa/Laura — flagging this as a 40% variance vs standard list pricing. Laura, I need a quick read on whether we can accept this for the forecast if the PO is received by 5/12.

If procurement can turn a PO by 5/12, customer indicated they will go to legal the week after. I plan to track this as "Late-Stage Opportunity - POC" in the pipeline until we have a signed DocuSign. Please advise whether to mark as COMMIT vs PROBABLE given the concession.

Attachments: EdgeCloud_SOW_v3.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer

Rishi / Laura — quick internal note. Customer indicated PO target 5/14; they like the terms but procurement will push back on a 40% off list concession. I asked them to confirm whether the concession is year-1 only; awaiting confirmation.

Action items I need:
- Rishi: can Deal Desk review the 40% concession and provide an approval matrix? If we can't approve 40%, what's the maximum exception we can grant without exec sign-off?
- Laura: if we accept a 40% concession and they PO by 5/14, do you want this marked as COMMIT for the May forecast or as CONTINGENT/PROBABLE? If COMMIT, please update the forecast ARR impact to reflect net revenue after concession.

I'm attaching a short spreadsheet with the pricing scenarios and the current forecast row we have for this account (forecast_recap_May2026.csv).

Attachments: discount_approval_form.xlsx, forecast_recap_May2026.csv

Thanks — this is time sensitive given month-end close.
Karthik

Subject: Re: Internal: Discount exception request + forecast impact (EdgeCloud / RDW-5892)

Karthik — thanks for the heads up and the spreadsheet. Reviewed with Deal Desk and Finance touchpoint:

Decision summary:
- We can approve a one-time concession up to 30% off list without exec escalation, provided the following conditions are met:
  1) Customer signs a 12-month minimum commitment (PO or DocuSign)
  2) Pricing at renewal reverts to standard list (no further automatic discount)
  3) Sales returns signed discount_approval_form.xlsx to deal-desk@redwood.ai at time of signature

I attached the signed exception stub for internal record (discount_exception_signed.pdf). Given these terms, mark the opportunity stage as "Commit - Contingent" and forecast as COMMIT only after we receive the signed PO/DocuSign and the completed discount form.

Karthik: if customer can push PO by 5/14, we will clear the 30% now — but 40% requires SVP approval and we don't have time in this window.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Deal Desk
redwood.ai

Thanks team — I reviewed Rishi's terms. From a forecasting and month-end control perspective:

- Action for Sales: mark RDW-5892 as "Commit - Contingent" in the CRM now. Move to full COMMIT only when we have the signed PO/DocuSign and the completed discount_approval_form.xlsx returned to deal-desk@redwood.ai.
- Forecasting: Finance will record the opportunity in May's pipeline as a "Contingent Commit" bucket with net ARR = list ARR * (1 - approved_discount). For the 30% approved exception that Rishi offered, please use net ARR = list ARR * 0.70.
- For internal reporting we need: expected billing start date, GL code for deferred revenue (I will default to REV-POC-2026 unless you provide another), and the DocuSign link once issued.

I'll reconcile the numbers once I receive the final signed form and the DocuSign envelope. For transparency, I'll add a line in the May forecast recap noting the discount bucket and link to the Deal Desk approval (HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345).

Please upload the signed SOW/PO to the Deal record and send me the final invoice terms. If procurement hits 40% pushback, escalate to Marissa for customer negotiation.
